intelligence.what_they_do: OpenWhispr makes open-source voice dictation, meeting notes, audio transcription, and related AI tools that can run locally or through cloud transcription.
intelligence.who_they_sell_to: Individuals and teams that need speech-to-text, meeting notes, and transcription, with an Enterprise plan for organizations needing SSO, SCIM, audit logs, retention controls, and support.
intelligence.bottom_line: OpenWhispr has a real public repo with 10,889 stars, 5 of 6 checked repos active in the last 30 days, and 3 listed in-person roles across engineering and marketing. The biggest unknown is business maturity: funding amount, runway, paid conversion, team size, and enterprise readiness are not answered by the fetched sources.

claims_checked.evidence: The GitHub data for OpenWhispr/openwhispr shows 10,889 stars and 1,423 forks.
No independent download counter, package analytics, store listing, or user metric was provided to confirm the 150k+ download claim.

claims_checked.claim: Available on macOS, Windows, Linux, and iOS
claims_checked.evidence: GitHub shows a Windows package manifest repo named winget-pkgs, Swift and Objective-C code that support Apple-platform work, and the main repo describes the app as cross-platform, but the fetched data does not independently confirm all four platforms including Linux and iOS distribution.
The public GitHub organization includes the main openwhispr repo described as a voice-to-text dictation app with local and cloud models.

claims_checked.claim: HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, GDPR
claims_checked.evidence: The fetched sources only show the compliance labels and a Trust Center link; certification reports, audit dates, or a DPA would settle this.

signals.signal: 5 of 6 checked GitHub repos had commits within 30 days, including the main openwhispr repo on 2026-11-06 and model-registry on 2026-11-04.
signals.why_it_matters: A candidate would likely join a product that is still being actively shipped, especially around the desktop app and model catalog.

signals.signal: The careers page lists 3 open roles: Founding Engineering Lead, Founding Engineer, and Social & Brand Growth Creator, all in person in San Francisco or Chicago.
signals.why_it_matters: The team is small enough that new hires would probably own broad scope, but the in-person and no-sponsorship constraints matter early.

signals.signal: The main GitHub repo has 10,889 stars and 1,423 forks as of the fetched data, matching the site’s 10.9k GitHub badge.
signals.why_it_matters: There is visible developer interest around the project, which can help with distribution but also raises expectations for support and roadmap clarity.

signals.signal: The product surface is expanding beyond dictation: pricing lists Agent mode, MCP integration, chat over your data, API access, CLI, mobile companion app, and meeting recordings.
signals.why_it_matters: Engineering work may span desktop, mobile, cloud transcription, integrations, and enterprise admin rather than a single dictation app.

signals.signal: The blog shows 2026 content aimed at compliance and workflows, including a HIPAA-compliant AI note takers article on August 11, 2026 and a Google Docs voice typing guide on June 26, 2026.
signals.why_it_matters: The go-to-market angle appears to include security-conscious users and SEO-driven acquisition, not only open-source distribution.

signals.signal: Recent press-like search results include WIRED on May 30, 2026 asking whether users need to pay for transcription software and How-To Geek on May 2 and May 23, 2026 covering free open-source apps.
signals.why_it_matters: External discovery may be growing through consumer and productivity coverage, but the fetched summaries do not prove deep company traction.

Engineering has 2 roles: Founding Engineering Lead and Founding Engineer.
